title: Relative normalization commutes with stalk base change
statement: Let $S,C,P$ be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $c:C\to S$ any morphism, $f:P\to C$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism, and $s\in S$. Set $a:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}\to S$, $L=C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and $g:L\to C$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $N_f\to C$ and $N_{P\times_C L}\to L$ be relative normalizations [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]. Then the canonical comparison $N_{P\times_C L}\to N_f\times_C L$, given by $f.\mathrm{normalizationPullback}(g)$, is an isomorphism. No normality, smoothness, Noetherian or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0307 (lemma-integral-closure-localize), 035I, 02KH; Normalization.lean smooth-base-change instance, affine comparison proof

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood B of s in S. All points in the image of Spec O_{S,s} generalize s, so they lie in B. Around each point of L=C times_S Spec O_{S,s}, choose an affine U of C contained in the inverse image of B. Its inverse image V in L is affine by the restricted cartesian square of affine schemes. On sections that square is a pushout. The stalk ring is the localization of Gamma(S,B) at the prime of s. Transport this through GammaSpecIso; base change of localization shows Gamma(L,V) is the localization of Gamma(C,U) at the image of the prime complement.

Qcqs flat base change identifies Gamma of the pullback of P over V with the tensor product of Gamma(L,V) and Gamma(P,f^{-1}U) over Gamma(C,U). The same comparison holds for the integral, hence affine, normalization morphism. In Lean both comparisons are isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right.

Apply integral-closure localization in its tensor-product form TensorProduct.toIntegralClosure_bijective_of_isLocalization, followed by the section-ring algebra equivalence and the affine normalizationObjIso maps. Check that this ring isomorphism is the app of normalizationPullback after both pushout maps, using normalizationObjIso_hom_val, toNormalization_normalizationPullback_fst and normalizationPullback_snd. Its restriction is therefore invertible. Zariski locality on the opens V proves the global assertion.
